newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW-US stocks up, no rate action by FOMC.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-US stocks up, no rate action by FOMC.

text.p: U.S. stocks surged after the Federal Reserve announced no change in monetary policy after its meeting in Washington, leaving interest rates unchanged.
U.S. economists had been split over whether the Fed would ratchet up short-term rates or leave them unchanged.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average erased erarlier losses and surged 30 points, or 0.41 percent, to 7259.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index rose four to 837.5.
Following are comments from U.S. stock market experts after the Federal Reserve made no announcement:
ROBERT FROEHLICH, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, KEMPER FUNDS:

-- "I'm amazed. It's hard for me to fathom, because with GDP growth of 5.6 percent and under five percent unemployment I thought for sure they would move. I think we're done for the year because I think this was (the Fed's) one chance.
-- "The outlook for stocks now is for the year is 'I'll see you at 8000' because there is really nothing ahead to drive a major correction at this point.
PIERRE ELLIS, SENIOR ECONOMIST, PRIMARK DECISION ECONOMICS:
-- The decision leaves "a cloud over the market."
-- "It's good for the market short term ... but it leaves some uncertainty about what the Fed is going to do long term."
-- "We can't really tell what they (the Fed) think, which ultimately means the markets will not know what do with this. We're going to be back to watching data piece by piece."
HARRY LAUBSCHER, A MARKET ANALYST WITH TUCKER ANTHONY:
-- "We're telling people to sell into the good news. Any rally will be short lived.
-- "Keeping the rates the same won't help the dollar. If it (the dollar) continues to weaken, that won't help the market."
CHARLES PAYNE, PRESIDENT, WALL STREET STRATEGIES
-- "We're not surprised. There just wasn't enought there to make the Fed raise rates. I think we are in the clear for right now but not totally out of it."

-- "The Fed has been pretty adamant about fighting inflation with a pre-emptive strike," Payne said. "Right now the market place is so competitive that it is keeping prices in check. But if there is any data which shows inflation needs to be addressed, I think the Fed will be very aggressive in their actions to stamp it out."

-- "We're bullish on stocks and this decision by the Fed could provide the impetus to carry us into the ballyhooed summer rally. Bigger-cap issues could lead the rally, but that will give way to buying in the smaller-capitalization issues."
